sections.title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening
sections.abstract: Assay-aware models combine crude and purified direct-to-biology screening data, and a prospective campaign used model-selected compounds to extend the measured ROS1 potency/selectivity frontier.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report synthesis and testing of 84 prospectively selected compounds; the strongest reported compound had ROS1 IC50 14.7 nM and 233-fold selectivity over TRKB. The arXiv comment lists the NeurIPS 2026 AI for Drug Discovery workshop.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say tailoring model objectives to each assay stage and sharing information across stages improves prediction from heterogeneous screening data and supports multi-objective compound selection.
sections.unique_caveat: The study uses one pyrimidine core and a kinase discovery program; the authors note the purified evaluation sets are small and call for broader chemistries and targets. These are compound-assay results, not clinical evidence.

sections.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
sections.abstract: LocoGen guides a frozen DNA diffusion model by protecting inferred motif positions and applying out-of-distribution damping to background sequence, seeking a balance of predicted activity, novelty, and plausibility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 per the arXiv comment; evaluated against held-out prediction oracles using a benchmark of about 700,000 enhancer sequences from HepG2, K562, and SK-N-SH cells, generating 640 sequences per method.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that localized guidance reaches a property–novelty–plausibility region that tested baselines miss, under their computational evaluation protocol.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational generation and re-scoring, not a wet-lab test of the generated sequences. The authors tested one masked-diffusion backbone and explicitly call for experimental validation and comparisons with other backbones.

sections.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
sections.abstract: Co$^2$ODE learns context-specific marker selection and a latent closure term to model signalling dynamics from single-cell phosphoproteomic measurements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The study uses a published mass-cytometry dataset across 30 single-gene overexpression contexts, reducing a 30-marker panel to a 10-dimensional state with predictive accuracy comparable to a full-panel neural ODE.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present conditional coarse-graining as a way to expose context-dependent marker selection while preserving prediction of a signalling readout.
sections.unique_caveat: Predictive fit does not identify the underlying network: the paper reports that prior scores can shift the inferred structure without materially changing fit, and its own limitations note that recovered couplings are not reproducible across seeds. The study is not a causal demonstration of network rewiring.

sections.title: Quantitative Ultrasound Characterizes Perfusion Trajectories in Healthy and Inflamed Gingival Wound Healing
sections.abstract: A longitudinal ultrasound analysis estimates gingival perfusion after extraction and compares healing trajectories at visits classified as healthy or inflamed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The cohort comprised 51 patients followed from two weeks to three months after extraction; ultrasound-derived perfusion was compared with laser-speckle imaging, and automated region segmentation had a reported mean Dice score of 0.98.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that velocity-weighted color-pixel density tracked perfusion changes and was higher at recovery visits classified as inflamed than at healthy visits.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small observational imaging cohort, not evidence of improved treatment decisions or patient outcomes. The reported laser-speckle correlation was not statistically clear in the inflamed visits.

sections.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling
sections.abstract: LoRACM adapts a pretrained consistency model with low-rank updates to estimate posterior distributions for total-body PET kinetic models across tracer, protocol, and modelling settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report three adaptation settings on simulated and human data, each trained with 50,000 simulated pairs; human estimates were compared with non-negative least-squares fitting.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report adaptation in under three hours on one A100 GPU, simulation agreement with MCMC reference posteriors, and human-data estimates comparable to fitting baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state the human cohort sizes, and agreement with a fitting baseline is not clinical validation or proof of improved patient care. The paper is submitted to a journal, not reported as accepted.

sections.title: PCR-ALERA: A PCR-ELISA analogue but antibody-free DNA detection system
sections.abstract: PCR-ALERA couples PCR-amplified DNA to an activator peptide that reactivates papain, producing a fluorescent readout without antibody handling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper describes a biochemical assay workflow and reports an overall run time of about four hours including PCR, directly relevant to DNA detection and assay design.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose an antibody-free microplate alternative to PCR-ELISA based on modified-nucleotide incorporation, click-linked peptide activation, and a fluorogenic papain substrate.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not report limits of detection, specificity, sensitivity, or head-to-head performance, so comparative analytical performance and clinical utility remain unestablished.

sections.title: Transmission and filtering of stochastic rhythms in bursty gene expression
sections.abstract: An analytical framework derives how degradation, transcriptional bursting, and upstream timing variability affect the transmission of stochastic regulatory rhythms to gene expression.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper derives autocorrelation and power-spectrum transmission relations and reports that its predicted degradation threshold separates all ten pulsing and non-pulsing p53 target proteins classified in earlier experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author proposes an analytical theory for conditions under which downstream genes preserve or filter stochastic rhythmic signals.
sections.unique_caveat: This is mainly theoretical; the ten-protein comparison uses previously published experimental classifications and does not supply new experimental validation.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Design methods paired with biological measurements: D2ML combines assay-specific prediction with prospective compound synthesis and testing. By contrast, LocoGen's DNA designs are assessed with computational oracles; the paper itself identifies wet-lab validation as a next step. These related design efforts have different validation levels. Learning biochemical dynamics without overclaiming mechanism: Co2ODE and the stochastic-rhythm analysis formalize signalling and gene-expression dynamics; Co2ODE exposes an identifiability problem in its phosphoproteomic data, while the rhythm theory checks a derived threshold against prior p53 classifications. Quantitative biomedical measurement and assay translation: the gingival-ultrasound and PET papers report human-data evaluations; PCR-ALERA describes a biochemical assay concept. The evidence ranges from an observational cohort to fitting-baseline comparisons and an assay workflow, not clinical-effectiveness studies.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: LocoGen: evaluate alternative generative backbones and test generated sequences experimentally; synthesize a prespecified set and measure expression in matched MPRA assays across represented cell lines with an independent evaluation oracle. Co2ODE: targeted perturbations that break correlations among candidate markers, followed by held-out prediction and independent pathway assays, could test whether selected markers are mechanistically informative. D2ML: repeat prospective selection across additional chemical scaffolds and targets with larger purified-compound sets. Ultrasound and PET: independent cohorts and multi-site/scanner repeatability studies would clarify robustness; report PET human cohort sizes and prespecify comparisons against reference methods. PCR-ALERA: measure analytical sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, reproducibility, and matrix interference against established PCR readouts.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest experimental result in this batch is D2ML's prospective compound synthesis and assay, but it remains a single-program preprint result. LocoGen and Co2ODE offer computational approaches while highlighting the need for wet-lab and intervention-based validation. The imaging, PET, and PCR papers report measurement or method development—not evidence of clinical benefit.
